speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your neck and arm pain, could you tell me exactly which fingers are experiencing the tingling sensation? Also, does the pain worsen when you turn your head or look up?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness specifically affect your grip strength or finger abduction, and do you notice any clumsiness with fine motor tasks like buttoning a shirt? I also need to know if you have experienced any changes in bowel or bladder control or balance issues.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine
REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS

Given the combination of neck pain, paresthesias, absent reflexes, and fasciculations, I need to rule out cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy, so please await these test results.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Cervical Spine: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region. EMG/NCS: Not performed/No data available.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of a syrinx explain your symptoms of pain, weakness, and fasciculations. Since the MRI was obtained after your motor vehicle accident, this is likely a post-traumatic syrinx causing syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
